h: Turn it into a full-blown science trail
p: Cambridge is a dream for anyone who's caught the science bug, because the university throws open a whole cluster of museums to the public, and many of them don't charge for general entry. That means you can turn an hour of hands-on experiments into a properly brainy day without breaking the bank.

The Museum of Zoology is a favourite with kids, with skeletons and specimens from right across the animal kingdom, while the Sedgwick Museum of Earth Sciences is stuffed with fossils, rocks and minerals. The Whipple Museum of the History of Science shows off old scientific instruments, and the Fitzwilliam Museum covers art and antiquities if anyone in the group needs a change of pace. Opening days vary between them, so it's worth lining up which ones are open on the day you visit.

For a breather, the Cambridge University Botanic Garden, a short walk south of the centre, has glasshouses and wide lawns that are perfect for a picnic. And of course there's the river: watching the punts drift past the colleges never gets old, even if you don't fancy taking a pole yourself.

A tip for families: Cambridge is best on foot or by bike, and parking in the centre can be a faff, so the Park and Ride is often the stress-free option. Pack snacks, comfy shoes and a notebook for the inevitable 'but how does that work?' questions.
